uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The recognition date is the settlement date, 17 June 2026. The valuation method is the telegraphic transfer buying rate of USD on the last day of the tax year, 31 March 2027. No TDS obligation arises as the amount is below the threshold. The penalty position is governed by s.439(8), requiring a bona fide explanation and disclosure of all material facts.

citation.provision: Section 115BBH, Income-tax Act, 1961 — carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025

regimes.reasoning: The receipt is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH, which taxes such transfers at 30%. The recognition date is the settlement date, 17 June 2026, as per Rule 56, Table Sl. No. 1. The valuation method is the telegraphic transfer buying rate of USD on the last day of the tax year, 31 March 2027, as per Rule 206, Table Sl. No. 3. No TDS obligation arises because the amount is below the threshold of ₹50,000 for individuals or HUFs, as per s.393(1), Table Sl. No. 8(vi). The penalty position is governed by s.439(8), which requires a bona fide explanation and disclosure of all material facts.
